exposure: Nasal Intermittent Positive Pressure Ventilation (NIPPV) only (control)
Poractant-alfa via INSURE-like method (bolus delivery) during NIPPV
Poractant-alfa via LISA using a nasogastric tube (NT) during NIPPV
Poractant-alfa via LISA using a vascular catheter (VC) during NIPPV
Poractant-alfa via LISA using the LISAcath R catheter during NIPPV
outcome: Pulmonary effects (pH, PaCO2, PaO2, dynamic compliance, total lung injury score, biochemical lung analysis, lung compliance, lung damage)
cohort: Spontaneously breathing newborn piglets (n=6/group) with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL)-induced respiratory distress.
finding: Less-invasive surfactant administration (LISA) techniques during NIPPV were well tolerated and efficacious in newborn piglets with respiratory distress syndrome, with vascular and LISAcath R catheters associated with better lung compliance and less lung damage compared to other methods, and no significant impact on brain injury scores across all surfactant administration techniques.
